statusDetail: Atomic audit completed across six representative paths. Video/podcast playback, ad-vendor click-through, authenticated account state, and destructive/commercial transactions were not covered because they are separate third-party or unavailable journeys; the selected pages cover the homepage, article, live data, league detail, search, and failure-state templates.

paths.description: Homepage and news portal template, including navigation, headline carousel, scores, ads, and news lists.
Representative news article and reading journey from homepage headline to article body.
Live-results application template, a high-value frequently updated task surface.
League table/detail template, representing structured sports statistics and navigation tabs.
Primary search flow using the homepage GET form with a common Persian query.
Representative unavailable route used to assess failure messaging and recovery.

findings.summary: The homepage forces a fixed 1122px desktop canvas instead of adapting to small screens.
findings.evidence: The layout primitive measured a 780px viewport against 1122px content (342px overflow); the viewport meta hard-codes width=1122, and the 390x844 screenshot shows the desktop page scaled to tiny text.
findings.suggestedFix: Use width=device-width and rebuild the homepage grid with intrinsic tracks, flexible sizing, and tested narrow breakpoints; do not shrink a desktop canvas to fit.

findings.summary: The visual theme does not meaningfully adapt to a dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-preference screenshot remains white/light gray and computed body background is rgb(255,255,255); no usable dark surface treatment is visible.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and define semantic surface/text tokens using prefers-color-scheme or light-dark(), preserving contrast in both schemes.

findings.summary: Auto-advancing animation is not reduced for users who request less motion.
findings.evidence: The probe found a running 15,000ms homepage animation and no prefers-reduced-motion rules; the reduced-motion capture showed no alternate static state.
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap non-essential animation in prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference and stop auto-advance under reduce while retaining manual controls.

findings.summary: High-contrast preferences receive no explicit adaptation.
findings.evidence: The combined high-contrast preference capture is visually unchanged and the stylesheet probe found no dedicated contrast/forced-colors handling.
findings.suggestedFix: Use system colors or forced-colors/prefers-contrast adjustments for essential controls and verify focus, carousel arrows, and score controls remain visible.

findings.summary: Page and content-state changes are abrupt and use no View Transition treatment.
findings.evidence: CSS/DOM probing across homepage, article, and live score found no view-transition usage; navigation reloads directly without a continuity cue.
findings.suggestedFix: Add progressive cross-document view transitions for page changes and same-document transitions for tabs/carousel states, with a no-motion path.

findings.summary: Long content pages provide static chrome rather than scroll-aware orientation.
findings.evidence: The homepage is about 7,838px tall, but its header is static and the feature probe found no scroll-state query or progress treatment.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact sticky header and optional article/page progress indicator that reacts declaratively to scroll state without obscuring content.

findings.summary: Advertising and dense chrome dominate the homepage before core news and scores.
findings.evidence: The desktop screenshot shows multiple large ad panels occupying much of the first viewport, while the mobile-fixed layout makes content and controls extremely small.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a first-viewport ad budget, reserve fewer predictable ad slots, prioritize headlines/live scores, and defer below-fold ad/media modules.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is invisible and many controls are undersized.
findings.evidence: The focus probe found outline-style none on all sampled focused links and 17 of 30 sampled homepage targets below 24px high; Lighthouse also failed target-size.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a high-contrast :focus-visible ring and enlarge interactive hit areas to at least 24px, preferably 44px for primary touch controls.

findings.summary: The homepage component system relies on a fixed canvas and exposes no container-query adaptation.
findings.evidence: The stylesheet probe found no container queries; the same content cards remain in a desktop multi-column composition at 390px while article/live-score templates adapt separately.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable cards container contexts and use size-aware styling so each card adapts wherever it is placed, with media-query fallbacks only where needed.

findings.summary: The primary search journey can return an empty result for a very common query without useful results.
findings.evidence: Submitting the actual GET form to /search?q=فوتبال produced “در حال حاضر محتوایی وجود ندارد” despite the site containing extensive football content.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix search indexing/query handling, preserve the submitted query, and provide ranked news/team/video results for common terms.

findings.summary: The empty search state gives no query-specific recovery or next step.
findings.evidence: The tested search page only states that content is unavailable and then falls into the generic footer; it offers no spelling guidance, filters, popular searches, or retry action.
findings.suggestedFix: Show the query, explain that no matches were found, suggest alternative terms and popular destinations, and keep editable search controls in context.

findings.summary: Mobile loading performance misses the LCP quality bar.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse performance scored 0.64 with LCP 6.9s, Speed Index 7.0s and TTI 19.9s; the controlled trace was faster but confirms load behavior varies materially by conditions.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the actual LCP asset, shorten critical dependency chains, defer non-critical ads/scripts, and monitor field LCP/INP/CLS by template.

findings.summary: Heavy scripting delays interactivity.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured 6.4s main-thread work and 1.5s JavaScript execution with 250ms TBT; the trace also captured an 81.96ms long task.
findings.suggestedFix: Identify heavy first- and third-party scripts, remove unnecessary work, split remaining tasks, and use scheduler.yield() with the documented fallback.

findings.summary: The homepage ships a large, image- and script-heavy network payload.
findings.evidence: HAR captured 136 requests and 4,219,583 transferred bytes (2,775,741 image; 1,055,344 script); Lighthouse measured 5,345KiB and 250ms render-blocking savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize only the LCP image, defer/lazy-load non-critical modules, improve cache lifetimes, and remove avoidable render-blocking resources.

findings.summary: Substantial unused CSS and JavaScript are delivered.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 593KiB unused JavaScript and 88KiB unused CSS, plus missing source maps for large first-party JavaScript.
findings.suggestedFix: Route-split widget bundles, load ad/score modules on demand, remove unused styles, and publish valid production source maps where policy allows.

findings.summary: Important controls and links lack accessible names or valid role relationships.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse accessibility scored 0.77 and failed link-name, select-name, aria-required-parent, and main-landmark audits; the probe found 120 empty-named links and many unlabeled selects/search controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Use semantic landmarks, label every form control, give icon-only links discernible names, and remove invalid ARIA role/parent combinations.

findings.summary: Text and essential UI fail minimum contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found examples including teal #0097a7 on white at 3.5:1 and white on #47a0c2 at 2.96:1, below the required 4.5:1 for small text.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust semantic color tokens to meet WCAG contrast in all themes and validate each state with automated and visual checks.

findings.summary: Reading structure and keyboard focus do not provide a dependable navigation model.
findings.evidence: The homepage has 74 headings but no h1, main or nav landmarks; sampled focused links all computed outline-style none.
findings.suggestedFix: Add one descriptive h1, main/nav landmarks and logical heading levels; implement a visible :focus-visible style and test a full keyboard walk.

findings.summary: Viewport and reflow settings restrict comfortable mobile and zoom use.
findings.evidence: The homepage fixes viewport width at 1122; article and league templates include user-scalable=no; Lighthouse failed viewport optimization and target-size.
findings.suggestedFix: Use width=device-width, remove user-scalable=no, support 200–400% zoom/reflow, and maintain adequately spaced targets.

findings.summary: The homepage logs live-data WebSocket errors.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse captured a SignalR exception and a wss://ksocket.varzesh3.com/live-v2 handshake failure with HTTP 503.
findings.suggestedFix: Handle live socket unavailability as an expected state, retry with bounded backoff, expose stale/offline status, and avoid uncaught console errors.

findings.summary: Image markup and delivery are inconsistent.
findings.evidence: The image primitive found 24 images without dimensions, 20 oversized images, 48 without srcset, 66 legacy-format images and 54 missing/empty meaningful alt candidates.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve image dimensions, serve responsive modern formats with srcset/sizes, and provide meaningful alt text where images communicate content.

findings.summary: Deprecated API use, BFCache blockers, missing source maps and DevTools issues reduce platform hygiene.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported one deprecation, six BFCache failure reasons including an unload handler, missing source maps, and inspector issues.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace deprecated APIs, remove unload handlers, review no-store usage, restore valid source maps, and resolve DevTools Issues findings.

findings.summary: The representative article lacks a canonical link despite otherwise strong article metadata.
findings.evidence: The article metadata probe returned no link rel=canonical, while JSON-LD points to a shorter mainEntity URL and the visible URL includes a slug.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit one absolute self-referential canonical URL per article and keep canonical, JSON-LD url/mainEntityOfPage, sitemap and redirects consistent.

findings.summary: Security policy is incomplete despite HTTPS, HSTS and clickjacking protection.
findings.evidence: Headers show CSP limited to frame-ancestors only, with no script/style/default-src restrictions; Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy are absent.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a nonce/hash-based CSP beginning in report-only mode, add strict Referrer-Policy and least-privilege Permissions-Policy, retaining HSTS/nosniff/frame protections.

findings.summary: The page has a large advertising and tracking footprint.
findings.evidence: The tracker audit found 13 third-party origins including Google Tag Manager and Yandex; Lighthouse found 17 third-party cookies and the HAR recorded extensive ad/analytics traffic.
findings.suggestedFix: Audit each vendor for necessity, obtain consent where required, remove redundant trackers, shorten retention, partition/limit cookies, and batch minimal analytics.

findings.summary: Defensive browser policies and cookie posture are incomplete.
findings.evidence: Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy are missing; all three observed Yandex-derived first-party cookies use SameSite=None, including two with 365-day lifetimes.
findings.suggestedFix: Set least-privilege browser policies and review whether SameSite=None and year-long analytics identifiers are necessary; prefer Lax/shorter retention where cross-site use is not required.

findings.summary: The PWA surface is installable but provides no observable cached offline fallback after load.
findings.evidence: The page links a manifest and has an activated service worker, but Cache Storage contained no entries after a settled homepage visit.
findings.suggestedFix: Add and test a minimal offline fallback for navigation and resilient stale data handling for core news/score surfaces; keep live status explicit.

findings.summary: The Persian document declares lang but omits explicit right-to-left direction.
findings.evidence: Homepage, article and live-score probes report html lang=fa and an empty dir attribute; logical CSS properties are present.
findings.suggestedFix: Set dir=rtl on the document root and preserve logical properties so reading order and layout remain robust for bidirectional content.

findings.summary: Asset delivery wastes substantial bytes.
findings.evidence: The image audit found 20 oversized images, 48 without responsive sources and 66 legacy-format images; Lighthouse estimated 1,589KiB image-delivery savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate responsive AVIF/WebP variants, use srcset/sizes, reserve dimensions, and deliver each editorial/ad image near its rendered size.

findings.summary: Third-party ads, trackers and media consume a disproportionate first-load budget.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 4.22MB over 136 requests; tracker evidence found 13 third-party origins and the first viewport is dominated by ads.
findings.suggestedFix: Define template budgets for third-party bytes/requests, defer below-fold ads, remove low-value vendors, and batch/deprioritize analytics.

findings.summary: Background analytics and advertising work is chatty and not visibly tied to the core task.
findings.evidence: Network evidence includes Yandex, GTM, Tapsell/MediaAd and 13 third-party origins during the initial load, while Lighthouse measured 6.4s main-thread work.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate analytics, batch events, defer background fetches until idle/consent, and stop work when the page is hidden.
